title: How Space Gets Its Colors
dek: Twelve images. Five wavelength families. One question: what does color mean when the eye cannot see the original light?
learningObjective: By the end of the Trail, a visitor should be able to distinguish visible color, mapped wavelength color, multi-observatory composites and inferred data overlays without treating any of them as less truthful.

steps.prompt: Is every color in an astronomical image captured as light?
What changes when the detector receives ultraviolet instead of visible light?
Which structures appear or disappear between visible and infrared views?
Why can one nebula have several different infrared portraits?
What does white mean when red and blue are data channels?
What is hidden inside the visible-light dust lanes?
What can two instruments contribute to one shared frame?
Can you separate X-ray structure from infrared structure before reading the caption?
Where do X-ray, optical and infrared observations overlap?
How does the image encode four infrared wavelength ranges?
What does false color actually claim—and what does it not claim?
How many physical stories can one composite hold without becoming one literal view?
